text: dsh-background-by-model 是 DeepSeek Harness 网页端的主题与壁纸插件。它在设置中加入界面、模型背景和配置页面，并按当前会话的模型名称匹配有序规则，让不同模型使用各自的壁纸与主题色。用户可上传图片或从网址添加图片，为规则配置多张图片、透明度、亮度、模糊和轮播，也可调整多个界面区域的透明度、导入导出配置并启用节日背景。配置和图片保存在本机 DSH 数据目录；推荐配置及节日图片会从 Bilibili 图片 CDN 下载。不需要 API 密钥。

dsh-background-by-model adds model-based wallpapers to DeepSeek Harness. Ordered rules match the session model to an image and accent color. Add images, tune opacity, brightness and blur, rotate wallpapers, and enable holidays. Settings are local; art downloads from Bilibili. No API key.

功能「模型背景规则」：按规则顺序将当前会话的模型文本与匹配词进行不区分大小写的包含匹配，使用首个命中规则；没有命中时回退到第一条可用规则。
功能「多图壁纸」：通过文件选择、拖放或图片 URL 为规则添加或替换壁纸，可重新排序、删除，并为每张图片单独设置显示模式和视觉效果。
功能「壁纸轮播」：为规则启用顺序或随机轮播，选择间隔，支持模型切换时前进一步；仅当前规则轮播，页面隐藏时暂停。
功能「界面透明度」：在 Interface 设置页分别调整主页区域、设置面板、聊天文字、轨迹页、右侧栏和插件页面的透明度。
功能「节日背景」：在内置节日日期窗口启用中秋或国庆背景覆盖；节日图片尚不可用或未启用时回到模型规则背景。
功能「推荐配置」：将内置的七条模型规则及对应壁纸应用为推荐主题；图片从固定的 CDN 地址下载，失败时支持重试和续传。
功能「主题导入导出」：把规则和图片打包成 JSON 配置文件，支持导入旧版本配置；插件将配置持久化到本机并迁移旧壁纸数据。
功能「图片存储清理」：查看本地壁纸占用及未被规则引用的文件，并清理孤立图片；插件在配置不可确认时拒绝按猜测清理。
dsh-background-by-model 使用推荐配置或节日背景时会从 Bilibili 图片 CDN 下载壁纸；自定义图片网址也由 DSH 主机下载。用户配置和上传图片则存于本机 DSH 数据目录。

dsh-background-by-model README · dsh-background-by-model：> Forked from [`Tkingxiao/dsh-any-background`](https://github.com/Tkingxiao/dsh-any-background) and renamed to `dsh-background-by-model`.

A **DeepSeek Harness** appearance plugin built around an **ordered list of model rules**: each rule carries its own images, and each image its own layout mode, framing, theme color, opacity, brightness and blur. Switch the model and the background switches with it, through the global [switch effect](#switch-effect-global) you choose on the Config page.

dsh-background-by-model README · dsh-background-by-model：> **v0.3.0 was a breaking release** — video wallpapers, generated backgrounds and the single global theme color were removed. See the [v0.3.0 entry in CHANGELOG.md](./CHANGELOG.md#v030).

---

dsh-background-by-model README · How Model Rules Work：A rule is a **match string** plus **one complete set of background settings**. On a model switch the plugin reads the current session's model name, scans the list top-down, and applies the **first** rule whose match string appears anywhere in it (case-insensitive) — with **rule 1** as the fallback when nothing matches.

Example list:

| # | Match string | Wallpaper |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `deepseek` | Image A |
| 2 | `flash` | Image B |
| 3 | `glm` | Image C |

dsh-background-by-model README · How Model Rules Work：| Current model | Result | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `DeepSeek-Flash` | Rule 1 → Image A | `deepseek` matches first |
| `GLM-Flash` | Rule 2 → Image B | `flash` is earlier in the list than `glm` |
| `Qwen-Flash` | Rule 2 → Image B | `flash` matches |
| `GLM-Turbo` | Rule 3 → Image C | only `glm` matches |
| `Kimi-K3` | Fallback → Rule 1 → Image A | no rule matches |

dsh-background-by-model README · How Model Rules Work：- **Order matters** — the first match wins, not the best match; drag rules to reorder them.
- **An empty match string** makes a rule skip matching and act purely as a fallback, so a single rule with an empty match string is "one wallpaper everywhere".
- The match string is compared against **provider, model id and display name** concatenated, so any of the three can select a rule.
- The current model is read from **this session's durable model selection** (the `modelSelection` projection the composer's own picker renders), so switching models inside a session takes effect immediately; the page shows what was read, and marks it **host default** when only the host-wide default was available.

dsh-background-by-model README · How Model Rules Work：> The example above has **no `kimi`** entry, so Kimi falls back to rule 1 = Image A and looks like "nothing happened" — add a rule with the match string `kimi`.

dsh-background-by-model README · Model rules：An ordered list of rules, matched first-hit against the current model's name, with rule 1 as the fallback.

dsh-background-by-model README · Model rules：- **Rules** — add, remove, reorder and name them; each carries its own match string, and a set of images with their own look.
- **Images per rule** — a filmstrip filled by file picker, drag & drop or a list of URLs; reorder it, promote one to first, or replace one in place (which keeps its position in the rotation). A rule may also hold none, and an empty rule still matches while it has a theme color of its own, so emptying one is a visible state rather than a trap.
- **Live match readout** — the Model Background tab shows which model was read and which rule it resolved to.
- **Import / export** — the whole rule set as `dsh-background-by-model-theme.json` with every image inlined; files written by earlier releases still import.
- **On disk, not in `localStorage`** — everything lives under `~/.dsh/.dsh-background-by-model-data/`, and old single-wallpaper configs migrate in place on first read.
- **Bilingual**, with automatic locale detection, plus a theme watchdog that re-asserts the theme if the host resets it.
dsh-background-by-model README · Image rotation：Per rule, and **off by default** — cycling spends real bandwidth, memory and battery, so nothing turns it on for you.

dsh-background-by-model README · Image rotation：- **Dwell time** — 10 s / 30 s / 1 min / 5 min / 30 min, or any custom value in seconds (5 s – 24 h).
- **Order** — **In order** walks the list and wraps around; **Shuffle** picks among every image except the one on screen, so a tick never looks like it was missed.
- **Also step on a model switch** — a second trigger that runs no timer at all.
- **Next image** — steps the wallpaper on demand, whether or not the timer is running.
- **Only the active rule rotates**, on one timer for the whole plugin; a hidden tab stops the rotation with the pixels.

dsh-background-by-model README · Switch effect (global)：What a wallpaper **change** looks like — one setting on the Config page, shared by every rule, covering a model switch, a rotation step, **Next image** and a holiday taking over.

dsh-background-by-model README · Switch effect (global)：- **Four effects** — **Cross-fade** (the default), **Instant**, **Zoom in** and **Slide in**; zoom and slide only animate `transform` on the incoming layer, so neither costs a byte of extra transfer.
- **Easing and one duration** — standard / linear / ease-out / ease-in-out, and `0`–`3000 ms` where `0` is a hard cut rather than "unset". It replaced the per-rule `rotate.fadeMs`, which had no control anywhere; a hand-tuned value is folded into it on first read.
- **Reduced motion is a veto**, not a shorter animation.
- **The interface color fades on the same clock** — except a light↔dark flip, which switches instantly, because interpolating between two palettes walks through mid-tones whose text is unreadable in both directions.
- **A preview swatch** replays the effect, because a wallpaper fading into itself is invisible.

dsh-background-by-model README · Holiday backgrounds：One switch on the Config page and nothing else: on 中秋节 and 国庆节 the wallpaper switches to that holiday's own art and theme color, and back the next morning. It ships **off**, and the [recommended profile](#recommended-profile) turns it on.

dsh-background-by-model README · Holiday backgrounds：- **中秋 is 农历八月十五**, resolved from the Chinese calendar in **Asia/Shanghai**, so it moves every year (2024-09-17, 2025-10-06, 2026-09-25 …); **国庆 is October 1–7**; when the two collide, 中秋 wins.
- **A holiday with no image falls through** to the model rules rather than blanking the wallpaper.
- **The art is downloaded, not shipped** — one compressed wallpaper per holiday, served by **Bilibili's image CDN** (`i0`/`i1`/`i2.hdslb.com`, three edges falling back to each other) and cached under `holiday-cache/<hash>/` on the first read of the day. The directory is named after the **content hash** in the URL: new art means a new address, therefore a new directory and a guaranteed re-download — there is no version constant to remember to bump. The download is gated on the calendar, so an ordinary day fetches nothing at all and every later boot is answered from disk.
- **Neither the art nor its palette is swappable** — a holiday slot is read-only, the colors and the full-bleed Fill mode come from the definition, and theme exports carry your rules only.

dsh-background-by-model README · Per-rule and per-image settings：- **Wallpaper** — one or more images per rule; the first is what the rule paints when nothing rotates.
- **Theme color** — HSL wheel, numeric input, **Extract from this image** and an eyedropper. It belongs to the **image**, and an image with none follows the system theme rather than inheriting its rule's.
- **Layout mode** — fit / fill / stretch / tile / center, stored per image; disabled on a rule that holds no picture, rather than hidden.
- **Framing** — drag to pan and scroll to zoom, editable in fit mode only, stored per image and stable across window resizes.
- **Image opacity** `0–100%`, **image brightness** `0–200%` (`100%` is the picture as saved) and **image blur** `0–60 px`, all three **saved per image** and edited through **one slider with a menu beside it** that picks the effect — so a daylight photo and a night shot in one rotation keep their own exposures. They treat the image (wallpaper) layer only; the Interface tab's opacity treats interface surfaces. A rule with no image has all three disabled rather than hidden.

dsh-background-by-model README · Global settings (Interface tab)：- **Opacity per interface part** — main background, left panel, right panel, cards & menus, input & controls, settings panel, conversation text box, trajectory page and every plugin page, each with its own slider.
- **A fresh install already looks like the author's own profile**, so a first run needs no download to look right.
- **Independent of the theme color** — a rule with no color keeps every one of these sliders live.

dsh-background-by-model README · Recommended profile：One click on the Config tab installs the author's own configuration — seven model rules and their interface numbers **ship inside the plugin**, and only the seven wallpapers are downloaded, from **Bilibili's image CDN**.

dsh-background-by-model README · Recommended profile：- **The rules are no longer a remote file** — they are compiled into the bundle, at the same version as the code that reads them. So this button does not need GitHub to be reachable, and there is no "the remote profile is newer than this build" case left to refuse: what gets installed is always what this build itself writes.
- **The wallpaper addresses are a constant table** — slot → BFS path, fixed at build time. The request set never comes off the network, so a wrong press cannot turn into "fetch 64 files because somebody else's document said so".
- **One address, one set of bytes** — a BFS path is a hash of the upload, so a wallpaper URL is immutable in a way a git tag is not.
- **`@3840w.webp` is load-bearing** — the uploads are 2.4–12 MB PNGs (76 MB for the set); with that suffix they are the 250–365 KB 4K WebPs an existing data directory already holds, byte for byte.
- **Every interface number in it is what the plugin already ships with**, so on a new install the button adds rules and pictures; on a store you have already tuned it resets those too, because it is a whole configuration and not a patch.

dsh-background-by-model README · Image storage cleanup：The last card on the Config tab. Images are stored at **full fidelity**, so an interrupted upload, a failed file deletion or a wholesale config replacement can leave a file on disk that no rule references any more — and on a tidy machine that number is normally **0**. The card reads the numbers, and the button deletes **without asking**.

dsh-background-by-model README · Image storage cleanup：- **Read first, delete second** — it shows how much is cleanable and how many files that is, before it offers the button. A cleanup whose size is announced afterwards is a cleanup nobody agrees to. The numbers describe only **what the press would free**: "2.1 MB in use" answers a question nobody asked on this card, and a total file count reads as "eight to delete" when the honest answer is one.
- **Only unreferenced files** — every byte a current rule uses is untouched, and the config itself is never written. The card re-reads after the sweep instead of subtracting, so a file that failed to delete still counts.
- **Failures are named** — one undeletable file does not protect the other six, and it is not reported as success either: the toast lists which ones.
- **No confirmation step** — what it deletes is by definition referenced by no rule, and is not a choice made from a working set, so a "confirm?" here only teaches people to click through. The safety is in the **gate**: when the config cannot be read the button is disabled (next bullet), rather than seven files being listed and then asked about.

dsh-background-by-model README · Storage：Data directory: `~/.dsh/.dsh-background-by-model-data/` (Windows: `C:\Users\<you>\.dsh\.dsh-background-by-model-data\`)

dsh-background-by-model README · Storage：| File | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| `theme-config.json` | The rule list (each rule with its image list, and each image with its own look and rotation settings) plus the global Interface settings, the global switch effect and the holiday overrides |
| `theme-config.json.bak` | The previous config, as of the last **successful** save. Every save writes a temp file and renames it over the live one, rotating the current good file into `.bak` first; a live file that will not parse is restored from here instead of falling back to the factory defaults. With neither readable, the cleanup card refuses to delete images |
| `modelbg-<slot>` | One image, stored as raw bytes without a file extension — one file per image, so a rule with three images owns three slots |

dsh-background-by-model README · Method 1: npm install (Recommended)：```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-background-by-model
```

This is the only source — a `github:` install would clone a tree with no `lib/` in it, and nothing there would build one.

Then restart `dsh web`.

The plugin appears as a **"Theme"** section in Settings.

dsh-background-by-model README · Method 2: npx (No Global Install)：```sh
npx @deepseek-ai/dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-background-by-model
npx @deepseek-ai/dsh web
```

dsh-background-by-model README · Method 3: Local Build (Development)：`lib/` is **not** in the repository — it is built from `src/`, by the package's `prepack` hook when the tarball is packed, and by you for a working copy. Clone, install, then build:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/HarmlessFunny/dsh-background-by-model.git
cd dsh-background-by-model
pnpm install
pnpm test            # builds lib/, typechecks, runs the thirteen checks

`pnpm run bundle` rebuilds `lib/` on its own. Either has to run before the plugin can load: a fresh clone has no `lib/`.

dsh-background-by-model README · Method 3: Local Build (Development)：`pnpm test` builds, typechecks and runs thirteen checks, none of which needs a dependency, a transformer or a browser. Each can also be run on its own with `pnpm check:holiday` / `pnpm check:rotation` / `pnpm check:transition` / `pnpm check:repaint` / `pnpm check:code-plate` / `pnpm check:image-mode` / `pnpm check:rules` / `pnpm check:preset` / `pnpm check:ui` / `pnpm check:watchdogs` / `pnpm check:scheme` / `pnpm check:store` / `pnpm check:node`:

dsh-background-by-model README · Method 3: Local Build (Development)：- **`check:holiday`** — the two holiday windows, the Beijing day boundary, leap eighth months across 1900–2100, and the four gates `pickHoliday` applies.
- **`check:rotation`** — `nextIndex` / `isRotating`: no walking off the end, shuffle never repeating the image on screen, and nothing called "rotating" with nothing to rotate.
- **`check:transition`** — `resolveFadeMs` / `transitionPlan`: the shipped default still producing byte-for-byte the transition string earlier releases wrote, every route to a hard cut being one, reduced motion vetoing rather than shortening, and every effect ending visible and unscaled.
- **`check:repaint`** — `shouldRepaint`, including the edit that **creates** the winner, plus a failure if any write path stops asking, or if a rotation step stops re-emitting the interface palette.
- **`check:code-plate`** — the code block's plate: its tokens declared on both `:root` and `body`, the light branch emitting the banner, and each surface reading its own plugin variable.
- **`check:image-mode`** — the lift onto the image for the layout mode and the three paint effects, and which image a control

dsh-background-by-model README · FAQ：**Every model looks the same — why?**
Rule 1 probably has an empty match string, which makes it a pure fallback holding the whole list. Give it a match string, or add more specific rules above it.

**`GLM-Flash` picked the wrong rule.**
Matching is first-hit, not best-hit: put the more specific rule higher in the list, or reorder.

**Where are my wallpapers?**
In `~/.dsh/.dsh-background-by-model-data/`, one `modelbg-<slot>` file per image plus `theme-config.json` and its `.bak` backup.

dsh-background-by-model README · FAQ：**What is `theme-config.json.bak`, and can I delete it?**
The previous config as of the last **successful** save. Every save writes a temp file and renames it over the live one, keeping the then-current parseable file as the backup — so if the live file ever stops parsing (a crash, a pulled cable, a hand edit gone wrong), the plugin restores from it instead of falling back to the factory defaults. You can delete it; the cost is having nothing to restore the next time the live file really is broken.

dsh-background-by-model README · FAQ：**I turned the rotation on and the background never changed.**
Three things can hold it: the rule needs two or more images, the tab has to be visible, and only the rule the current model resolved to rotates.

dsh-background-by-model README · FAQ：**Does rotating cost anything?**
Yes, which is why it is off by default: each image is stored at full fidelity and every switch repaints the whole interface. Two to five images is the sweet spot — boot only reads each rule's first image, so the cost is memory and disk rather than start-up time.

dsh-background-by-model README · FAQ：**Why did the theme color stop working after I removed a rule's images?**
That was the old behaviour, and it is fixed: a rule now counts while it has **an image, or a theme color of its own**, so it still matches and still serves as the fallback while painting the interface alone.

dsh-background-by-model README · FAQ：**I updated the plugin and the panel says my edits are not being saved.**
The browser half and the host half update separately, so a refreshed page can run the new client against DSH's process still running the previous node half, which cannot read the new config shape. The client holds its writes until you restart DSH.

dsh-background-by-model README · FAQ：**I set a color for one image and the other images did not change.**
That is the design: since 0.7.1 a theme color belongs to the **image**, so a rotation can move through pictures with different accents. A rule with **no image at all** is the one case where the controls edit the rule's own color.

dsh-background-by-model README · FAQ：**Where did the theme color I set before this update go?**
Nowhere: an image written before per-image colors has no `color` key at all, which is how the loader tells "never had one" from "cleared on purpose", and it lifts the rule's color onto every such image.

**Can I share a setup?**
Yes — export it from the **Config** tab; the JSON inlines every rule's image.

**Are video or generated backgrounds supported?**
No. Both were removed in 0.3.0; each rule uses a static image.

dsh-background-by-model README · FAQ：**After switching a rule back to "System theme", why is the settings dialog a different palette?**
That was a bug and it is fixed: every surface is now driven by one palette source, so clearing the color reads the host's own tokens back and re-emits them with your alpha.

dsh-background-by-model README · FAQ：**Why does "Custom color" produce a color the moment I press it?**
Pressing it means leaving the system-theme state, so it has to hand out a starting color — it runs the extract-from-image pass first and falls back to a default swatch only when the image has nothing vivid.

dsh-background-by-model README · FAQ：**After switching back to "System theme" the interface stays light until I drag a slider — why?**
The other half of the same bug, also fixed: the plugin forces `body[data-ds-dark-theme]` while it owns a color, and the host only rewrites that flag when it projects a theme snapshot. The switch now hands the flag back synchronously, and a one-second watchdog re-reads the host palette.

dsh-background-by-model README · FAQ：**I picked a new switch effect and the wallpaper still cuts instantly.**
The effect is **Instant**, or the duration is `0` — an effect and a duration are two ways of asking for the same hard cut, and the effect wins. Outside the plugin, a system **reduced motion** setting means nothing animates at all.

dsh-background-by-model README · v0.10.0：- **The config is written atomically, with a `.bak` of the last good file** — a save writes a temp file and renames it over the live one, keeping the previous parseable file as the backup; a corrupt live file is restored from it instead of falling back to the factory defaults and then being overwritten by your next drag.
- **Opacity, brightness and blur are saved per image** — the same layer as the layout mode, framing and theme color; a schema-9 config's rule-level values are lifted onto every image on read, so nothing changes on screen.
- **`SCHEMA_VERSION` is 10** — the fields moved, and an older host would drop them in silence, so the browser half has to know.
- **A blurred wallpaper no longer paints a dark rim around the viewport** — the layer's box is grown 2σ past the screen edge and clipped, with the framing moved back by the same amount, so the blur samples off screen instead of fading into the page behind it.
- **A switch between two different opacity, brightness or blur values animates now** — each layer keeps its own picture's filter, and the wallpaper's opacity rides the transition instead of snapping.
